summary: Petition under Section 142 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulations 65 and 70(2) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023 for the execution of order dated 25.11.2024 passed by the Commission and directions and initiation of appropriate action against the Respondent for non-compliance of the directions issued under order dated 25.11.2024 in Petition No. 75/MP/2022. execution and enforcement of the Commission’s order dated 25.11.2024 in Petition No. 75/MP/2022, and initiation of appropriate action against BSES Rajdhani Power Limited (BRPL/ Respondent No.1) for non-compliance with the directions issued therein. - _“(a) Execute the Order dated 25.11.2024 passed by this Hon’ble Commission in Petition No.75/MP/2024;_ - _(d) Pass an order of attachment, attaching to the extent of Rs. 15,114,117/- from the bank account(s) belonging to the Respondent No.1/BRPL, pending disposal of the Petition;_ - _(e) Award costs of these proceedings against the Respondent and in favour of the Petitioner; and_ 7. In view of the disputes, the Petitioner, along with TPTCL, filed Petition No. 75/MP/2022 before this Commission, inter alia, seeking adjudication of the issues relating to the computation of LD, levy of GST on LD, and wrongful withholding of amounts by BRPL. iv. The Petitioner has also filed Appeal No. 91 of 2025 before the Tribunal challenging certain findings in the order dated 25.11.2024, including the findings relating to the levy of LD and the issue of GST. The said Appeal is presently pending adjudication before the Tribunal. However, the pendency of the appeals does not affect the enforceability of the Commission’s Order in the absence of any stay granted by the Tribunal. 11. After hearing the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission admitted the Petition and directed issuance of notice to the Respondents and parties to complete their pleadings. 13. Despite notice, none appeared on behalf of the Respondents. After hearing the submissions made on behalf of the Petitioner, the Commission reserved its order in the Petition. 16. The dispute between the parties in Petition No. 75/MP/2022 pertained to, _inter alia_ , the computation of LD for the alleged shortfall in supply of power under the Letter of Intent dated 13.2.2021 issued by BRPL to TPTCL, with the Petitioner being the source of supply. The Petitioner and TPTCL had contended that the permissible deviation of 15% from the contracted energy was required to be computed on a monthly basis, whereas BRPL computed the LD on a fortnightly basis, resulting in the deduction of excess amounts from the payments due to the Petitioner. On 25.11.2024, the Commission passed its order in Petition No. 75/MP/2022, partly allowing the issues raised therein, to the extent of directing that the computation of LD be undertaken on a monthly basis. The relevant portion of the order dated 25.11.2024 reads as follows: 19. However, it is well settled that the mere pendency of an appeal does not render the directions of the Commission unenforceable unless the operation of such directions has been specifically stayed by the appellate forum. In the present case, no stay has been granted by the Appellate Tribunal against the order dated 25.11.2024, and therefore, the said order continues to remain operative and binding upon the parties. 20. We observe that despite notice in the present proceedings, BRPL has neither appeared nor filed any reply rebutting the submissions made by the Petitioner. Accordingly, the averments made by the Petitioner regarding non-compliance of the directions contained in the order dated 25.11.2024 remain uncontroverted. ## _**“Section 142 – Punishment for non-compliance of directions by Appropriate Commission.**_ _In case any complaint is filed before the Appropriate Commission by any person or if that Commission is satisfied that any person has contravened any of the provisions of this Act or the rules or regulations made thereunder, or any direction issued by the Commission, the Appropriate Commission may after giving such person an opportunity of being heard in the matter, by order in writing, direct that, without prejudice to any other penalty to which he may be liable under this Act, such person shall pay, by way of penalty, which shall not exceed one lakh rupees for each contravention and in case of a continuing failure with an additional penalty which may extend to six thousand rupees for every day during which the failure continues after contravention of the first such direction.”_ Act or any directions or orders of the Commission shall invite appropriate action against the concerned party under Section 142 of the Electricity Act, 2003. 25. In this regard, the APTEL in Bihar State Electricity Board v. Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Appeal No. 53 of 2009, Judgment dated 31.7.2009) has clarified that proceedings under Section 142 are civil in nature and that the element of mens rea is not required to be established for invoking the said provision. The Tribunal observed that once the Commission is satisfied that its directions have been violated, appropriate action under Section 142 may be initiated after providing an opportunity of hearing. 29. Having considered the submissions of the Petitioner and the material placed on record, it is evident that the directions issued in the order dated 25.11.2024 have not been complied with by BRPL. In the absence of any stay against the said order, BRPL is bound to comply with the directions contained therein. 31. The Petitioner is at liberty to revive the matter in case BRPL fails to pay the abovesaid amount to the Petitioner within the specified period.
title: Petition under Section 142 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulations 65 and 70(2) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023 for the execution of order dated 25.11.2024 passed by the Commission and directions and initiation of appropriate action against the Respondent for non-compliance of the directions issued under order dated 25.11.2024 in Petition No. 75/MP/2022. Jindal India Power Ltd.
